title: vcap conformance report
description: What an implementation publishes to claim it passes a vcap-spec vector corpus. The claim is checkable only if it names the corpus (version and manifest hash) and how many vectors it actually ran: `vectors_run` must equal `vectors_declared`, and a report with `vectors_run: 0` is a failed run whatever `failed` says. See vectors/CONFORMANCE.md.

implementation.description: What was measured, precisely enough to be re-run by someone else: name, and where the verifier lives.

implementation_version.description: Version or commit of the implementation the report is about.

corpus_version.description: vectors/VERSION of the corpus the run used, e.g. "1.0.0".

manifest_sha256.description: SHA-256 of vectors/MANIFEST.json as committed. The version names a release; this names the bytes.

vectors_run.description: How many vectors the run actually executed. Zero is a failure, never a pass, and a value below vectors_declared is a partial run that must be reported as such rather than as conformance.

failed.description: One entry per vector whose verdict did not match expected.json. Published, not omitted: a report that only lists successes is not a measurement.

not_run.description: Vectors the implementation deliberately did not run, each with the reason. A runner that cannot exercise a vector kind says so here instead of lowering vectors_declared.

by_kind.description: Count of vectors run per vector kind (file, container, segments, jcs).

by_expected_outcome.description: Count of vectors per expected outcome, so a reader sees what the corpus is made of and not only how much of it passed.
